title: Internal-Hom comparison for finite-Tor constructible inputs
statement:
Let $X$ be a finite-type $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-scheme,
let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the site comparison,
let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A_{E,n})$, and let
$M\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A_{E,n})$. Then

$$
\nu_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\longrightarrow
R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K,\nu_X^*M)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, with the coefficient conventions in the statement. Finite type over $k$ makes $X$ quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover] gives a finite affine open cover $j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow X$. Each $U_i$ is of finite type over $k$: [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] says that its coordinate ring is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, and the single affine chart is a finite cover in the definition of finite type. Its structure morphism is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. We will apply the separated comparison theorem on these $U_i$; no assertion that intersections of affine opens of $X$ are affine is needed.

source.place: Proof, sentences 1-2: finite affine cover and reduction to separated schemes

proof.text: Restriction to an open subscheme is localization of either small site at that open object: an object over $U_i$ is precisely an etale, respectively weakly etale, $X$-object equipped with a factorization through $U_i$. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] this restriction is exact. Therefore it commutes with cohomology, computed as kernels modulo images, and preserves the cohomological bounds. Intersecting a constructible stratification with $U_i$ preserves its finite locally constant restrictions; hence $K_i=K|_{U_i}$ and $M_i=M|_{U_i}$ are bounded constructible, using [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. To check finite Tor amplitude without any assumption on $M$, choose a bounded flat model $P$ for $K$ using the etale-site clause of [lem-sf-flat-model]. Restriction carries its quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism, and each $P^r|_{U_i}$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat]. The converse flat-model implication on $U_i$ gives $K_i\in D^b_{ctf}(U_{i,\mathrm{et}},A)$ with the same interval.

source.place: Localization discussion before Tag 08FI, label lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; flat-model and slice-flatness statements cited explicitly

proof.text:
On either ringed site the canonical identification
$$R\mathcal Hom(K,M)|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom(K|_U,M|_U)$$
follows directly from the Hom-complex model. Choose a complex $L$ representing $K$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of $M$, as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $I|_U$ is K-injective. The formulas in [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identify both ordinary sheaf Hom restrictions by relocalization; products are sectionwise, so [def-pur-hom-complex] identifies both Hom complexes term by term, with the identical differential $d_I f-(-1)^n f d_L$. This proves the displayed derived identification, natural in both variables, without asserting a stalk formula for derived Hom.

source.place: Tag 08JB, label lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U; its proof using Tag 08FI

proof.text:
The comparison pullback also commutes canonically with open restriction. To see the actual identification, write $j_{	au,*}$ for direct image from $U_	au$ to $X_	au$, given by $(j_{	au,*}G)(V)=G(V	imes_XU)$, for $	au=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$. The restriction/direct-image adjunction follows by sending a natural map $F|_U	o G$ to its components $F(V)	o F(V	imes_XU)	o G(V	imes_XU)$, and recovering the former map at objects already over $U$. The formula $(
u_*G)(V)=G(V)$ on etale $V$ in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] gives, componentwise,
$$
u_{X,*}j_{\mathrm{proet},*}=j_{\mathrm{et},*}
u_{U,*}.$$
Consequently the two left adjoints $j_{\mathrm{proet}}^*
u_X^*$ and $
u_U^*j_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ have the same Hom bijections, giving the canonical isomorphism between them (the unique map corresponding to the identity of the common right adjoint). Exactness of $
u^*$ [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] and of restriction makes this the same identification on complexes and derived categories.

source.place: Proof, sentence 1: site comparison restricts to open subschemes (adjunction calculation written out)

proof.text:
Under the identifications of steps 3 and 4, the canonical comparison $\beta_{X,K,M}$ is defined as the transpose of evaluation. The derived tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], together with exactness of comparison pullback from [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], identifies this transpose with
$$
u_X^*R\mathcal Hom(K,M)\otimes_A^L
u_X^*K\longrightarrow
u_X^*(R\mathcal Hom(K,M)\otimes_A^LK)\xrightarrow{
u_X^*\mathrm{ev}}
u_X^*M.$$
Choose K-flat representatives of the tensor arguments by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective target as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The resulting comparison is therefore the evaluation-defined map used in the theorem.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 0A90 (lemma-compose), and evaluation calculation for the canonical comparison

proof.text: The tensor-Hom bijection in the preceding transpose is computed on each site using the complex currying isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total]. The Hom complex from a K-flat complex into a K-injective one is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] identifies its zeroth derived global sections with the derived Hom group. For the K-flat representatives with flat terms chosen in step 5, restriction preserves K-flatness with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the localization morphism of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Restriction preserves K-injective models by step 3, and the displayed currying and evaluation maps are componentwise the same after restriction: on a homogeneous tensor $f\otimes x$ evaluation is $f(x)$. Hence the adjunction identification from step 4 respects units and counits, so the restricted transpose is exactly the comparison map $\beta_{U,K|_U,M|_U}$.

source.place: Tags 0A96 (lemma-RHom from K-flat into K-injective), 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), and 08JB (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U); evaluation compatibility

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] on each $U_i$. Its separated finite-type hypothesis was checked in step 1, and its first and second input hypotheses in step 2. The coefficient is exactly the same finite stage $A_{E,n}$, with $\ell\ne p$ as in the fixed conventions. Its statement says that the canonical evaluation-defined map $\beta_{K_i,M_i}$ is an isomorphism. By steps 5 and 6 this is the restriction of $\beta_{X,K,M}$ to $U_{i,\mathrm{proet}}$. We use only that lemma's internal-Hom assertion; its dualizing-object and biduality assertions are unnecessary.

source.place: Proof, sentences 3-5: invoke the internal-Hom assertion of the separated finite-stage comparison

proof.text: Finally fix $r\in\mathbf Z$ and apply $\mathcal H^r$ to $\beta_X$. Exact restriction commutes with these cohomology sheaves, so steps 6 and 7 give an inverse on every $U_i$. These inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness of a two-sided inverse. For every pro-etale object $V\to X$, the opens $V\times_XU_i$ cover $V$; the sheaf axiom glues the local inverse maps uniquely, and their two composites are the identity since they are so on this cover. Therefore $\mathcal H^r(\beta_X)$ is an isomorphism for every $r$. The cohomology detection criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied to the abelian category of pro-etale $A$-module sheaves, proves that $\beta_X$ itself is an isomorphism. If $X$ is empty the sheaf axiom for the empty covering gives the same conclusion, so the argument also covers the empty affine covering.

source.place: Proof, sentence 1: locality of isomorphisms, with the sheaf gluing argument made explicit
